[LLSU.7.1] Service invocation via the (domain, method) dispatch table.
A response arrives as a fact of the service's response schema
([LCRS.4.3.1]) the rule can match in a sibling rule.

| Name | Explanation | Dependencies | Refactor hint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call` | `call <domain>.<method> args ...` action | | not generally avoidable; this is the fundamental external-effect primitive |
| `service_response_decl` | `response T` or `no response` as a service declaration's last line | `call` | not avoidable; every service declares its response |
| `call_response_fact` | the response fact, a `ttl` fact of the service's response schema matched on `corr` in a sibling rule | `service_response_decl` | requires re-designing around cache-based polling; usually a sign the tier is wrong |
| `call_error_fact` | `CallError e where e.corr == "<id>"` matchable in a sibling rule | `call` | silently swallow errors (usually wrong) |
| `call_correlation_explicit` | `as "<id>"` on `call` to set correlation id | `call` | accept compiler-generated corr ids (harder to grep in logs) |
| `call_cooldown_required` | `cooldown: <dur>` mandatory on every `call` (compile error if omitted) | `call` | not generally avoidable; this is the rate-limit safety |
| `nocooldown` | the bare `nocooldown` flag, the explicit opt-out for naturally-bounded calls | `call` | use a minimum cooldown value the tier's rate budget tolerates |
| `call_retain` | `retain: <dur>` on a call — refused on every call in this edition ([LCRS.6.3.3]) | `call` | none: a response's lifetime is its schema's TTL ([LCRS.6.6.1]) |
| `call_batch_coalescing` | adapter-side opportunistic batching of multi-entity calls | `call` | write per-entity calls; adapter coalescing is transparent, so disabling here just disables the optimisation |
